zones.what: Oceanview category OK and guarantee category OX cabins on decks 4 and 8 sit beside the lifeboat/tender stowage and are officially sold as fully or partially obstructed.
zones.effect: The lifeboat sits right outside the window; some of these cabins have frosted glass that cannot be seen through at all, while others just have a boat hull filling part of the frame. The horizon above the boat is usually still visible.
zones.mattersTo: View-focused guests and photographers should avoid OK/OX; budget-focused cruisers who just want daylight and a lower fare are the target market for this category and generally don't mind.
zones.source: cruisemapper.com and cruisedeckplans.com (OK/OX obstructed by lifeboats, frosted-glass warning); cruiseline.com (OK found on Deck 4 and Deck 8); cruiseline.com OX review ('obstructed view really is obstructed by a life boat...but you do get some daylight')

zones.what: Deck 11 suite categories (S4, M1, MA, MB, MX) sit directly beneath the Deck 12 Body Waves Fitness Center, which is part of the same pool/spa/buffet complex.
zones.effect: A guest in Suite 11518 reported hearing treadmill runners and dropped free weights 'liked war missiles' directly overhead during afternoon naps, and that gym use started around 5:00am.
zones.mattersTo: Guests wanting an afternoon nap or early sleep should ask whether their suite falls under the weights area; those who don't nap during the day may not notice.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com member review of Suite 11518 on Norwegian Jewel ('we both realized our beautiful, extremely expensive suite was directly beneath the fitness center')

zones.what: Deck 6 midship houses the Jewel Casino, Le Bistro, and several bars; Deck 5 cabins directly below are Oceanview/Inside staterooms in categories O4, OB, OF, IF, and IT.
zones.effect: Cruisers specifically ask about noise levels in cabins under the casino, suggesting late-night activity/foot traffic from slot machines and bar service can carry down.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers who retire early should be cautious of deck-5 midship; night owls unaffected by casino sounds may not care.
zones.source: cruiseline.com deck-by-deck listing (Deck 6 = Jewel Casino, Deck 5 = O4/OB/OF/IF/IT cabins); cruisecritic.com forum thread titled 'How noisy? Cabin under Casino-Jewel'

zones.what: The Stardust Theater's upper level occupies part of Deck 7 midship, directly beneath Deck 8 balcony category BD cabins.
zones.effect: A Cruise Critic poster specifically asked whether BD balcony cabins on deck 8 are noisy at night because they sit over the theater; deck-plan confirms the theater's top tier is on deck 7 below.
zones.mattersTo: Guests who want to be in bed during evening showtimes should ask about BD category specifically; those out at the shows themselves won't be in the cabin to notice.
zones.source: cruiseline.com deck-by-deck listing (Deck 7 = upper level Stardust Theater); cruisecritic.com forum thread 'Jewel balcony Cabin on deck 8' asking about BD category noise over the theater

zones.what: A cruiser in a far-forward Deck 4 cabin on Norwegian Jewel's transatlantic crossing reported hearing the anchor chain and engine noise clearly.
zones.effect: Far-forward, low-deck cabins pick up anchor-drop rumble every port morning and general engine/mechanical sound transmitted through the hull.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and those sensitive to mechanical noise should avoid the extreme forward end of Deck 4; those who like white noise or don't mind early anchor sounds may be fine.
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com forum ('We heard the achors, the engines, everything... Loved the ship, hated the cabin location')

zones.what: Forum guidance specific to a Norwegian Jewel deck-4 booking question notes pitching (up-and-down motion) is more noticeable at the forward and aft ends of the ship, and thrusters create noise/vibration while docking.
zones.effect: A far-forward Deck 4 cabin will feel more pitch in rough seas and more thruster noise/vibration during every docking maneuver than a midship cabin on the same deck.
zones.mattersTo: Motion-sensitive cruisers should pick midship over forward on the lowest deck; those who don't get seasick and don't mind mechanical hum during arrivals/departures can disregard.
zones.source: cruiseaddicts.com forum on Norwegian Jewel deck 4 ('Pitching...is more noticeable at the forward and aft ends of the ship, and the thrusters will create lots of noise and vibration when maneuvering in and out of dock')

zones.what: NCL's own stateroom page states plainly that the two Deck 15 suites (numbered 15500 and 15000) do not have elevator access.
zones.effect: Guests booked in these top-deck suites must use stairs to reach their room; there is no elevator serving Deck 15 at all.
zones.mattersTo: Mobility-limited guests or anyone with heavy luggage should avoid or specifically confirm accessibility for these two suites; able-bodied guests seeking the top-deck view may not mind the stair climb.
zones.source: ncl.com official Norwegian Jewel deck plans page ('*Suites on deck 15 (15500 and 15000) do not have elevator access')

zones.what: Multiple Norwegian Jewel cabins are booked directly adjacent to or across from elevator lobbies (e.g., cabin 8588 near elevators on deck 8-mid, cabins 11572/11574 directly across from the elevator on deck 11).
zones.effect: Proximity to elevators is a recurring booking question on Jewel; general cruise-line guidance also flags elevator-adjacent cabins for foot-traffic and door-chime noise, though no confirmed noise complaint was found for these specific cabins.
zones.mattersTo: Guests prioritizing quiet should ask for cabins a few doors down the hall from a bank; guests prioritizing easy access (families, mobility needs) often prefer these locations.
zones.source: cruisecritic.com forum threads on Norwegian Jewel cabins 8588 and 11572/11574 near elevators; elliestraveltips.com general guide advising against elevator-adjacent cabins

leads.claim: Suite located directly beneath the Deck 12 fitness center/weights area; guests reported being woken by treadmill and weight noise starting around 5am.
Obstructed oceanview cabin on deck 8-mid, described by the booked guest as 'close to the elevators.'
leads.source: cruisecritic.com forum 'How noisy? Cabin under Casino-Jewel'

leads.claim: Adjoining cabins located directly across from an elevator bank on deck 11; guest asked whether this would hurt privacy/create noise (no confirmed answer found).
leads.source: cruisecritic.com forum 'Jewel Cabin near elevator - Is this a Plus or Minus?'

leads.claim: Accessible/handicapped oceanview room with an unusual layout: one large undivided bathroom, L-shaped room, beds that cannot be joined, and only a hard chair (no comfortable seating).
leads.source: cruisedeckplans.com stateroom detail notes for Norwegian Jewel cabin 8100

leads.claim: Booked as an 'enclosed balcony' category with no clear explanation found by the guest of what that means versus a standard open balcony.
leads.source: cruisecritic.com forum 'What is an enclosed balcony on the Jewel?'

leads.claim: Balcony category BD on deck 8 sits above the Stardust Theater's upper level; a guest asked whether these cabins are noisy at night from the shows below (unanswered in the thread found).
leads.source: cruisecritic.com forum 'Jewel balcony Cabin on deck 8'

unknowns: Whether Deck 9 balconies directly above the Deck 8 lifeboat line have any view-down obstruction; NCL does not appear to officially label a deck-9 obstructed category on Jewel, but no source confirmed or denied a partial sightline block for the two decks above the boats.

Exact deck and route of the Norwegian Jewel's crew-only 'I-95' corridor; NCL fleet-wide use of this corridor is confirmed generically, and it is documented running the length of Deck 4 on the larger Breakaway-class Norwegian Getaway, but no Jewel-specific source locating it was found.

Whether Jewel-class balconies have any cantilevered 'hump' sections that extend past the hull line; no first-person or class-specific source (as opposed to generic aggregator boilerplate) was found supporting this for the class.

The 'In Hull'/metal-enclosed forward balcony claim from cruisedeckplans.com appears verbatim on Norwegian Dawn, Norwegian Star, and Norwegian Gem deck-plan pages regardless of class, indicating boilerplate template text; it was discarded as unverified for Jewel-class specifically per the control-check rule, so true forward hull-taper balcony geometry for this class remains unconfirmed.
Bow thruster noise/vibration reports specific to Norwegian Jewel deck 8 forward cabins (a relevant-looking Facebook thread was found but not accessible for verification).
Whether connecting-cabin ranges or specific accessible-cabin ranges beyond deck 8 (cabin 8100) carry any class-wide quirks.
